---
title: CLI
---

Run the installed command through uv:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --help
```

Commands that use a repository require a configuration file. Pass the global
options before the command:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --config config.yaml generic list
uv run restic-backups --config config.sops.yaml --sops generic list
```

The equivalent environment variables are `RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG` and
`RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1`. See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for setup.

## Root commands

| Command | Purpose | Remote storage |
|---|---|---|
| `check-config` | Load and validate configuration | No |
| `generic ...` | Run generic configured repository commands | Depends on subcommand |
| `voice-memos ...` | Run the macOS Voice Memos workflow | Depends on subcommand |

## Generic commands

| Command | Purpose | Remote storage |
|---|---|---|
| `generic list` | Show backup IDs, stores, endpoints, and enabled state | No |
| `generic data-dir [BACKUP]` | Print the managed private-data directory | No |
| `generic init` | Initialize each enabled referenced repository once | Yes |
| `generic run --backup ID ...` | Pass trailing arguments directly to restic | Depends on restic command |

`generic data-dir` and `generic run` prompt with Questionary when the backup is omitted from an
interactive terminal. Non-interactive callers must provide the ID.

## Restic passthrough

Use `generic run` for any repository operation not represented by a higher-level
workflow command:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup voice-memos snapshots
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup voice-memos check
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup voice-memos restore latest --target /tmp/restore
```

The CLI loads the selected store, exports credentials and restic repository
settings only to the child process, and does not print them.

## Managed data directory

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic data-dir voice-memos
```

The result follows
`data/<store-id>/<bucket>/<key-prefix>/<backup-id>/`. It is intended for
private generated metadata, not as a required root for backup source files.

## Cold S3 guard

`GLACIER_IR` behaves as immediate storage. For `GLACIER` or `DEEP_ARCHIVE`, the
CLI permits uploads but blocks retrieval-related work unless both the restore
policy is valid and `ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1` is set. The configured tier,
days, and timeout are then passed to restic's S3 restore support.

Commands outside the explicitly guarded cold-storage set are rejected. Use
`GLACIER_IR` for repositories requiring normal interactive restic access.
